section: Solar energy - PV vs thermal technologies, National Solar Mission, solar parks, rooftop solar, ISA

accepted.s: The original target fixed for the Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission was subsequently revised to which level?
accepted.x: The National Solar Mission initially targeted 20 GW and the target was subsequently enhanced to 100 GW.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original target from the subsequently revised target.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Solar Park Scheme:
1. It was launched on 12 December 2014.
2. Its initial objective was to develop more than 25 solar parks with an aggregate capacity of 20 GW in five years.
3. The target was enhanced to 40 GW on 21 March 2017.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The scheme was launched on 12 December 2014, initially envisaged over 25 parks and 20 GW, and was raised to 40 GW on 21 March 2017.
accepted.tq: Use the date and revised target to verify all three statements.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Solar Park Scheme?
o: It exclusively provides standalone solar pumps to farmers up to 2025-26.
It finances only rooftop systems in urban households up to 2026-27.
It provides land, transmission infrastructure and statutory clearances for solar parks and is scheduled to run up to 2025-26.
It establishes nuclear parks with compulsory battery storage.
accepted.x: The Solar Park Scheme facilitates land, transmission and clearances for solar parks and runs up to 2025-26.
accepted.tq: Identify the scheme from its package of infrastructure and clearance support.

accepted.s: Solar parks developed under the Solar Park Scheme generally have a capacity of approximately:
accepted.x: The scheme envisages solar parks of about 500 MW or more each.
accepted.tq: Test the scheme-specific capacity threshold.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: VGF schemes—Viability gap funding for grid-scale solar developers
CPSU Scheme Phase-II—Standalone solar pumps only
PM-KUSUM Component B—Solarisation of grid-connected pumps
accepted.x: VGF schemes, including JNNSM Phase-II arrangements through SECI, provide viability gap funding to grid-scale solar developers. Component B concerns standalone pumps, while Component C concerns grid-connected pump solarisation.
accepted.tq: Separate the purposes of closely related solar schemes.

accepted.s:
With reference to PM-KUSUM, consider the following statements:
1. Component A relates to decentralised or small grid-connected plants on barren land or farmland.
2. Component B concerns standalone solar pumps.
3. Component C concerns solarisation of grid-connected pumps.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe Components A, B and C of PM-KUSUM.
accepted.tq: Match each component letter with its distinct field application.

accepted.s: According to the progress reported up to 30 November 2025, which one of the following is correctly matched with PM-KUSUM?
accepted.x: By 30 November 2025, Component A had recorded 667.31 MW. Component B had 9.42 lakh pumps and Component C had 10.99 lakh solarised pumps.
accepted.tq: Use the unit difference—MW for Component A and pumps for Components B and C—to eliminate traps.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding PM-KUSUM progress is correct?
o: Component A recorded 9.42 lakh MW of capacity.
The reported achievement for Component B was 9.42 lakh pumps, against a figure of more than 9.75 lakh cited for the 2025-26 estimate.
Component B had already crossed 20 lakh pumps by 30 November 2025.
Component C concerned only off-grid pumps and had no solarisation target.
accepted.x: The reported Component B achievement was 9.42 lakh pumps, while the Economic Survey 2025-26 cited more than 9.75 lakh in the relevant context.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an achievement figure from a separately cited estimate and check the units.

accepted.s: The CPSU Scheme Phase-II primarily seeks to promote solar plants by:
o: Farmers installing only diesel-powered irrigation pumps
Private households using imported rooftop modules without subsidy
State governments constructing floating solar plants without domestic-content requirements
Government entities using viability gap funding and domestically manufactured cells and modules
accepted.x: CPSU Scheme Phase-II supports government producers through viability gap funding and domestic cells and modules.
accepted.tq: Ask who implements the scheme and what technology-content condition it carries.

accepted.s: How much solar capacity had been commissioned under CPSU Scheme Phase-II in 2025?
accepted.x: Approximately 2.87 GW had been commissioned under CPSU Scheme Phase-II in 2025.
accepted.tq: Protect the decimal and unit from a magnitude trap.

accepted.s: Which scheme was subsumed into PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana?
accepted.x: The Rooftop Solar Programme Phase-II, launched in 2019, was subsumed into PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana.
accepted.tq: Trace the successor scheme rather than confusing schemes with similar solar objectives.

accepted.s: The Production Linked Incentive scheme for high-efficiency solar modules, introduced in 2021, is primarily associated with:
o: Construction of solar parks on barren land
accepted.x: The 2021 PLI scheme for high-efficiency modules promotes domestic manufacturing.
accepted.tq: Link the policy instrument to its industrial objective.

accepted.s: SRISTI is associated with which of the following?
o: Rooftop solar incentives, the ARUN app and Suryamitra skilling
Nuclear fuel enrichment and reactor safety
accepted.x: SRISTI is associated with rooftop incentives, the ARUN application and Suryamitra skill development.
accepted.tq: Recognise a multi-component programme from its distinctive app and skilling links.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about PM Surya Sarovar Yojana:
1. It was approved on 31 July 2026.
2. It targets 5,000 MW of floating solar capacity by 2030-31.
3. The scheme requires two-hour battery storage.
4. SECI is to implement the scheme.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. PM Surya Sarovar Yojana concerns floating solar, has a 5,000 MW target by 2030-31, mandates two-hour battery storage and is to be implemented by SECI.
accepted.tq: Check the date, target, storage condition and implementing agency together.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly associated with PM Surya Sarovar Yojana?
o: An outlay of ₹75,021 crore and support of ₹1 crore per household
A target of 20 GW of solar parks by 2025-26
An outlay of ₹5,070 crore and support of up to ₹1 crore per MW
A target of 30 GW of residential rooftop solar by 2026-27
accepted.x: PM Surya Sarovar Yojana has an outlay of ₹5,070 crore and provides support of up to ₹1 crore per MW.
accepted.tq: Separate the financial figures of similarly named solar programmes.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the reported installed solar capacity and its share of total capacity?
accepted.x: The reported installed solar capacity was 157.05 GW, constituting about 29 per cent of total capacity.
accepted.tq: Pair the capacity figure with its percentage instead of mixing figures from different reporting dates.

accepted.s: India added a record solar capacity of approximately how much in financial year 2025-26?
accepted.x: A record 44.61 GW of solar capacity was added in FY 2025-26. The 2.82 GW figure relates to the earlier 2014 level, while about 38 GW refers to the 2025 addition in another comparison.
accepted.tq: Distinguish annual additions from historic benchmark and cross-country comparison figures.

accepted.s: The Energy Survey 2025-26 places India at which position globally in solar energy and total renewable energy?
accepted.x: The Energy Survey 2025-26 places India third globally in solar energy and total renewable energy. Other publications cited different rankings for solar, so the source-specific wording is important.
accepted.tq: Follow the named source when rankings differ across publications.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's solar-sector growth:
1. India was the second-largest solar growth market in 2025.
2. India's approximately 38 GW addition in 2025 exceeded that of the United States for the first time.
3. India had added only 2.82 GW of solar capacity in 2014.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. India was the second-largest solar growth market in 2025, its approximately 38 GW addition surpassed the US for the first time, and the 2014 addition was 2.82 GW.
accepted.tq: Combine a ranking, a comparison and a historical numerical benchmark.

accepted.s: Which of the following shows the correct chronological order of cumulative installed solar capacity?
accepted.x: The sequence is 63.30 GW on 31 December 2022, 132.85 GW in November 2025, 150.26 GW on 31 March 2026 and 162.15 GW on 30 June 2026.
accepted.tq: Arrange the figures by their reporting dates before comparing their magnitudes.

accepted.s: As of 30 June 2026, which composition of cumulative solar capacity was reported?
o: 125.6 GW utility, 30.11 GW off-grid and 6.43 GW rooftop
125.6 GW rooftop, 30.11 GW utility and 6.43 GW off-grid
125.6 GW off-grid, 30.11 GW rooftop and 6.43 GW utility
125.6 GW utility, 30.11 GW rooftop and 6.43 GW off-grid
accepted.x: The 162.15 GW total comprised 125.6 GW utility-scale, 30.11 GW rooftop and 6.43 GW off-grid capacity.
accepted.tq: Match each capacity figure with its segment rather than merely ordering the numbers.

accepted.s: Which place became the first Union Territory to run entirely on solar power during the daytime?
accepted.x: Diu became the first Union Territory to run 100 per cent on solar power during the day.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Union Territory first from airport and village firsts.

accepted.s: Modhera in Gujarat is recognised as India's first:
accepted.x: Modhera, the Sun Temple town in Mehsana district, became India's first 24x7 solar-powered village.
accepted.tq: Match the place with the exact first, avoiding nearby solar superlatives.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about Modhera's solar project is correct?
1. It has a 6 MW solar plant.
2. It includes a 15 MWh battery energy storage system.
3. It was opened on 9 October 2022.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Modhera's project includes a 6 MW plant and 15 MWh battery storage system and was opened on 9 October 2022.
accepted.tq: Verify the capacity, storage size and inauguration date as separate details.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Cochin International Airport—World's first fully solar-powered airport
Diu—First Union Territory to run 100 per cent on solar power by day
accepted.x: Bancha is India's first all-solar-kitchen village and is located in Betul, Madhya Pradesh; it is not a Union Territory. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped category in an otherwise familiar list of solar firsts.
